w: In the morning, Swamishri went for darshan to the Sanatan Dharma Mandir, which is the oldest in Uganda.
At 12.30 pm, the Vice-President of Uganda, Prof. Gilbert Bukenya, came to meet Swamishri.

The vice-president requested, “I believe that you are the centre of unity for the world. The world gains inspiration from you. Please give blessings that Uganda progresses and that unity and prosperity increases.” Swamishri conveyed his blessings. The meeting lasted 30-minutes, during which various topics were discussed.

At 4.17 pm the solar eclipse commenced. During the assembly, Viveksagar Swami spoke on the significance of eclipses. Finally in his blessings Swamishri said, “There are three types of miseries: adhyatma, adhibhut and adhidev. Whenever one faces miseries one should always pray and chant the name of God. God dissolves all our worries and pains.” The solar eclipse concluded at 5.35 pm.

In the evening the secretary of Jaipur Development Authority Shri Himatasinh, Additonal Advocate General of Rajasthan Shri Bharatbhai Vyas and minister of PWD Shri Rajendrasinh Rathod met Swamishri and received his blessings.

? In the afternoon 275 women devotees took out a kalash yatra procession carrying auspicious pots in the mandir neighbourhood. ? In the evening an assembly was arranged to felicitate devotees who had rendered their services for the shikharbaddh mandir. Swamishri first presented a shawl to Jaisukhbhai Jhala for handling the construction work and thereafter blessed the prominent devotees. Finally, blessing the devotees and 700 BAPS volunteers, Swamishri said, “It is a matter of great happiness that a lot of people have come from Gujarat and other areas to seek the spiritual benefit of this festival. To get such opportunities to offer seva in functions like these turn out to be of immense spiritual advantage. It is service to God and if God is pleased, you are blessed. You will attain God’s abode and become happy. When you work for others it is for the sake of your body, whereas this service to God is for the benefit of your soul. With such service you attain the bliss of God’s Akshardham. You will have great peace. When God is pleased, your birth becomes worthwhile.”

Rakeshbhai of Umreth is observing dharna-parna vrat since last four years. Girishbhai Alaiya of Finchley is observing waterless fast every Friday for Swamishri’s health. He is also observing dharna-parna vrat since last four-and-a-half years and pilgrimaging by foot every Saturday to the mandir.

In the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, on 3 October 2010, youths of the current batch attending the Youth Training Centre in Sarangpur presented an inspiring program during the evening Sunday assembly. Based on theme ‘Bharat Bhagya Nirmata’, the youths conveyed the message that if India is to fulfill its true potential on the world stage, youths will have to contribute through service, values and spirituality. The training centre youths presented an excellent program including a discussion, debate, traditional dance and other presentations.

On entering the lift to come down from the mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj must have read the sign: "Only for handicapped". In that context, Swamishri said to Yogvivekdas Swami, "We are using the wrong lift. This is for the disabled."
Yogvivekdas Swami explained, "There is no problem for you."
Swamishri constantly insists on observing even the smallest rules.

Brahmamangaldas Swami said to Mahant Swami Maharaj, "I have noticed one thing: whenever you give blessings over the phone, you say, 'These are the blessings of Swamibapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj), and our prayers.' But you never say, 'These are our blessings.'"

His attempt was to bring out that Swamishri keeps his guru foremost. But Swamishri turned the answer in a completely different direction: "Our blessings are already included in Swamibapa's blessings."
Hearing this, Atmaswarupdas Swami said, "That we consider them separate is a flaw in our understanding."
Agreeing, Swamishri said, "It is a matter of understanding."
Returning after completing his walk, Mahant Swami Maharaj saw a youth named Harsh holding the door of his room and asked, "You are two brothers?"
"Yes."
"One is sitting there (watching the walk), isn't he?"
"Yes."
Once again we experienced Swamishri's subtle power of observation.
